brief.angle: If a context window degrades accuracy by 1% for every 1,000 words processed, reading a 50,000-word book reduces key detail recall by exactly 50%.
brief.measure: Linear reduction of accuracy across long text inputs.
brief.calc: 50,000 words / 1,000 words = 50 steps; 50 steps * 1% loss per step = 50% cumulative loss.

spec.title: Why long context windows lose accuracy
spec.summary: Processing a 50,000 word input degrades accuracy by 50 percent through cumulative linear loss.
sources: Assumed degradation rate of 1% per 1,000 words

beats.say: Reading a fifty thousand word book deletes half of its facts.
The system loses one percent accuracy every one thousand words.
Fifty thousand words equals fifty steps of text.
Each step drains accuracy at the same steady rate.
At one thousand words, input accuracy drops to ninety nine percent.
At ten thousand words, ten percent of details disappear.
At twenty five thousand words, twenty five percent vanishes.
At fifty thousand words, fifty percent is missing entirely.
That is twenty five thousand forgotten words.
The missing details are not randomly chosen.
Longer prompts simply erase the beginning of your text.
Feeding a full novel guarantees a fifty percent coin flip.
The longer you talk, the less it remembers.
